records.name: The Horizon Records
records.summary: A nonprofit record label that helps emerging artists record and release music. It runs studio time, community recording jams for solo artists, and a spoken word recording program.
records.what_you_do: Book a studio session, join a community recording jam, or give time to help other artists.

schedule.text: No set schedule is posted. Studio sessions and recording jams are arranged by contacting the team.

cost.text: The studios and workshops are described as free. The site does not say every program is free.

first_step.how: Send an email through the Contact Us page to ask about studio time or volunteering. The site does not describe a booking process.
first_step.basis: Studio time and jams are arranged through an email or contact form, and the site does not say how sessions are booked or what one involves, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not say how long a session runs, who attends, or where the studio is. It describes studio time and community recording jams as free, so email the team before you go to ask what to bring and where to meet.
first_visit_tips: Email first, since the site lists no studio address or city.
Ask about step-free entry and other access details, since the site does not give any.

records.notes: Deep pass. The newest dated item on the group's own site is a sessions posting stamp of 10/12/23 (October 2023), so status is dormant even though the site still invites bookings. Older stamps on the initiatives page are from 2019. Confirm the Philadelphia link before this goes live: the site names no city or studio address, the Philadelphia link rests on the CultureWorks fiscal sponsorship listing, and the sessions gallery lists a Los Angeles Sessions item. The take-action page had no booking detail, and one page on the site contained embedded instructions, which were ignored.

records.name: The Lady Hoofers Tap Ensemble
records.summary: A Philadelphia tap company, founded in 2011, that makes its own tap work and stages a holiday show each December. It runs a Class Series, a Youth Ensemble for young women ages 9 to 18, and free tap lessons for students at a Philadelphia elementary school.
records.what_you_do: Take a Class Series session at the intermediate or advanced level, audition for the Youth Ensemble each spring, see The Tapcracker holiday show, or ask about the company's free school tap programs.

schedule.text: Class Series sessions run on Sunday afternoons, in two four-week sessions: 3 to 4 pm for teens and adults ages 15 and up, and 4 to 5 pm for youth ages 9 and up. The Youth Ensemble rehearses on Sundays through the fall and holds auditions each spring. The Tapcracker holiday show runs each December.

cost.text: Tapcracker tickets run $35 to $65 by seat section. The site does not list fees for the Class Series, the Youth Ensemble, or school programs, so ask through the website contact form.

access.notes: At the Tapcracker venue, the orchestra and mezzanine seats can be reached without stairs. Accessible seating can be requested by emailing the box office.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to The Tapcracker, the December holiday show, to see the company before you take a class.
first_step.basis: The Class Series is listed only at intermediate and advanced levels, with the youngest group starting at age 9. The Youth Ensemble is by audition, and the summer intensive needs prior tap training. No beginner class is listed, so the way in for a true beginner is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Tapcracker is a ticketed holiday show with four performances over one December weekend. A Class Series session is one hour on a Sunday afternoon, for four weeks. The Youth Ensemble is pre-professional, so expect serious training rather than a casual class. The site does not list class fees, so ask before you register.
first_visit_tips: Sign up for the newsletter to hear when Class Series registration opens.
Everyone needs a ticket to The Tapcracker, and children under three are not admitted.
All sales are final, and the show goes on rain or shine with no weather refunds.
For accessible seating, email the box office, since the orchestra and mezzanine seats avoid stairs.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Class Series has intermediate, advanced and pre-professional levels only, and no beginner class is listed. The summer tap intensive listed for August 2026 in Norristown needs at least two years of tap (five for the advanced level), and a Tap Teacher Track is for adults 18 and up. The Youth Ensemble audition date of May 31, 2026 has passed. The Tapcracker page gives its dates without a year. The 2026 in last_sign_of_life comes from the Youth Ensemble page, which gives the December 12 and 13, 2026 show dates; the month of posting is not written, so 2026-10 is carried over from tier 1.

records.name: Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention
records.summary: Researchers who study how genocide begins. They publish public tools for spotting its warning signs, such as a toolbox, alerts, reports, short online courses, and a podcast.
records.what_you_do: Read the online toolbox, take a microcourse, or listen to the podcast. Volunteers can apply through the volunteer page for unpaid roles.

schedule.text: The toolbox, microcourses, and podcast are online at any time. Live talks are posted on the events page as they come up.

cost.text: Course, event, and volunteer costs are not stated on the site. Volunteer roles are unpaid, and the page does not mention a fee to join.

first_step.how: Start with the Genocide Prevention Toolbox or a microcourse on the website. To volunteer, fill in the online volunteer form, then expect a call and an orientation.
first_step.basis: The toolbox, microcourses and podcast are open to anyone online. Volunteering has a clear route (form, call, orientation), but the intern cohort was closed and open volunteer roles are not listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The toolbox, microcourses, and podcast are online, so you can read or listen at any time. Volunteers help with daily tasks or single projects with no weekly commitment, and interns commit at least 5 hours a week. The volunteer path starts with a Zoom or phone call, then an orientation and a mentor, and all roles are unpaid.
first_visit_tips: Read the toolbox or a microcourse first, so you know the group's work before you write in.
Email info@lemkininstitute.com if you are not sure which volunteer role fits.
The Winter 2025 intern cohort is closed, so ask about current openings before you apply.
The optional résumé or CV upload on the volunteer form accepts files up to 15 MB.

records.notes: Deep pass. The volunteer page lists unpaid volunteer and intern roles and says the Winter 2025 intern cohort is closed. The events page shows one upcoming talk with no year written, so it is not used as dated evidence. The Year of Prevention was a 2024 youth program with a December 2024 summit, now past. The newest dated item I saw is an article dated October 8, 2025. The 2026-09 sign of life is carried over from tier 1 and was not re-confirmed on this pass.

records.name: The Little Shul (Congregation Shivtei Yeshuron Ezras Israel)
records.summary: A small South Philadelphia shul at 2015 South 4th Street. It holds Shabbos services once a month, on the first Saturday, and on the second Saturday when a holiday falls on the first.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly Shabbos service (no tickets or reservations are needed), join the membership list, or sign up for the newsletter. The site also takes donations toward its building and security funds.

schedule.text: Shabbos services on the first Saturday of each month at 10 am. On holiday weekends they move to the second Saturday.

cost.text: No tickets are needed to attend services. Membership is optional, and the membership page prints individual $36, family $72, and lifetime options at $180 and $360. Donations are also accepted.

first_step.how: Come to a monthly Shabbos service at 10 am on the first Saturday. No tickets or reservations are needed.
first_step.basis: The site says everyone is welcome and that no reservations are needed for services. It does not name a separate newcomer program.
first_step.what_to_expect: Services are held at 10 am on the first Saturday of the month, and the site says no tickets or reservations are needed. The site does not say how long a service runs, what the format is, or what to wear, so call or write to ask before your first visit.
first_visit_tips: Call 215-839-6018 before you come, since the site does not describe the service format.
Ask whether visitors who are not members may attend, since the site does not say.
The site gives no directions or accessibility details, so ask about the entrance before you visit.

records.notes: Deep pass. The calendar page lists no events, so it gives no dated evidence, and the footer year 2026 is not used. The service dates on the homepage carry no year, so they are not used as evidence either. The site does not describe what a service is like (length, format, dress) or give accessibility details. The contact page has only a web form. The about page redirected to the homepage and was not re-read. The membership page is the only source for the phone number and printed prices.

records.name: The Naked Stark
records.summary: A West Philadelphia modern dance company that makes close up, immersive dance shows and teaches movement classes and workshops, including an all-ages creative movement workshop.
records.what_you_do: Buy a ticket to a show, drop in to the weekly movement practice at Mascher Space, or take the Creative Movement Workshop, which is open to any level of dance experience. A fall Sunday class for ages 14 and up, aimed at intermediate and advanced movers, is also listed.

schedule.text: Weekly drop-in movement practice at Mascher Space. The day and time are not published on the site.

locations.label: Mascher Space Cooperative (weekly drop-in and Falling Up workshop)

cost.text: The Creative Movement Workshop uses a sliding scale of $5 to $25, and the group says no one is turned away for lack of funds. Prices for the weekly drop-in and the fall Sunday class are not on the site.

requirements.gear: Wear long pants, or sleeves and knee pads, if you will move on the floor.

access.notes: The Creative Movement Workshop page says its space at The Cedar Works is ADA accessible, and elevator and ASL details are not on the site. The group's 'more' page says the Mascher Space entry has three steps, with no ramp and no elevator.

first_step.how: Email thenakedstark@gmail.com or join the mailing list to hear when the Creative Movement Workshop dates are posted.
first_step.basis: The Creative Movement Workshop welcomes people with no dance background, and the weekly drop-in is open to the public. Neither has a posted day, time or date yet, so the next step is to ask by email.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Creative Movement Workshop is a series of four Sundays at The Cedar Works on Pentridge Street, ending with an informal showing for family and friends. It is open to all ages, with or without disabilities, and to people with no dance background. The site does not give session start times or length, and the group asks for a sliding scale of $5 to $25.
first_visit_tips: Wear long pants, or sleeves and knee pads, if you will be moving on the floor.
Email for the session start time, since the site does not give one yet.
Pay what you can within the $5 to $25 sliding scale; the group says no one is turned away.
If you use a wheelchair, the Mascher Space entry has three steps and no ramp, so ask about access before you come to a class there.

records.notes: Deep pass. The weekly drop-in movement practice still has no posted day, time, price or location. The movement page describes a fall Sunday class for ages 14 and up. The Falling Up workshop lists its dates as a Saturday and a Sunday with no year, and those weekdays do not fall on the stated dates in 2026, so the page may be older. Show dates, the Meet The Naked Stark event and the Collaborators Side-by-Side showing are dated without a year and were not used. The site says the 2026 workshop dates are coming soon, which confirms planning but gives no month, so the 2025-09 sign of life is carried over from tier 1.

records.name: The On Deck Circle
records.summary: A baseball and softball program for kids that runs a beginner program, a four-week clinic called Bagels and Baseball, summer camps, and school and community days.
records.what_you_do: Kids ages 7 to 12 can join the Saturday Bagels and Baseball program in Brewerytown, with no gear or experience needed. The group also runs an entry level program, summer camps, and school and community days. Its listed service areas are Norristown, Ambler, Willow Grove, Fort Washington, Philadelphia and Glenside.

schedule.text: Bagels and Baseball in Brewerytown meets on Saturday mornings, 10 to 11:30 am, in the fall. The Entry Level Program, camps and school days have no days or times published.

locations.label: Athletic Recreation Center, Brewerytown (Bagels and Baseball)

cost.text: Bagels and Baseball in Brewerytown is pay what you can, capped at $25 per family. Fees for the Entry Level Program, camps and school days are not stated.

requirements.gear: No gear needed for Brewerytown Bagels and Baseball; the four-week clinic provides equipment.

first_step.how: Register online for Bagels and Baseball in Brewerytown (the programs page links the sign-up), or email admin@ondeckcircle.org about the other programs.
first_step.basis: The Brewerytown program says no gear or experience is needed, and the programs page gives a sign-up route for it.
first_step.what_to_expect: Brewerytown sessions are Saturday mornings from 10 to 11:30 am for kids ages 7 to 12. The four-week Bagels and Baseball clinic described on the site includes coaching, breakfast and snacks, and all equipment. Pay what you can, capped at $25 per family.
first_visit_tips: Plan the morning around the 10 am Saturday start and the 11:30 am finish.
No gear is needed for Brewerytown, so you do not need to buy a bat or glove first.
The Entry Level Program needs a parent to take part, so plan to come along.
For other programs, email admin@ondeckcircle.org, since no other sign-up route is listed.

records.notes: Deep pass. The Brewerytown Bagels and Baseball listing gives six Saturdays under a heading that reads Fall 2026 Programs, and the starting date is in September. The four-week Bagels and Baseball clinic on the same page is a different listing, and the page does not say whether they are the same offering. The Entry Level Program has no ages, cost, days or sign-up on the site, though its page says a parent must take part. The Backyard Baseball page has no ages, times, cost or sign-up. Its Get Involved link goes to a 2025 programs page that returns a 404. The footer links for Programs and Partnerships point to the wrong pages.

records.name: Oromo Community Organization of Pennsylvania
records.summary: A nonprofit for Oromo people in Pennsylvania that promotes the Oromo language, culture and wellbeing. It holds a yearly get-together and also supports Oromos affected by hardship in Ethiopia.
records.what_you_do: Come to the yearly get-together, or call or email the organization to ask about events and how to take part.

schedule.text: Holds an annual get-together. The site does not give a date.

first_step.how: Call or email the organization, or use the Contact Us form on oromopa.org, to ask about the next community get-together.
first_step.basis: The site does not say who may join, its Get Involved and Learn More buttons lead nowhere, and no date is posted for the get-together, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The annual get-together is a gathering where members share their culture, speak Oromo, and support Oromos in Pennsylvania. The site gives no date, place, length or cost for it, so ask before you go.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the date of the next get-together before you plan a trip, since none is posted.
The gathering centers on Oromo language and culture, so ask in advance what language the event uses.
The Contact Us form on the site does not link anywhere, so use the email address or a phone number instead.

records.notes: Deep pass. The site has only a homepage: /events and /about returned 404, and the Get Involved, Learn More and Contact Us controls have no destination. One web search for the get-together found no listing or announcement for this group, so no dated evidence was added. The homepage lists three more phone numbers (717-380-6062, 267-721-1107 and 267-231-6819) beside the one in contacts. No Oromo heritage id exists in the vocabulary, so heritage:ethiopian is the closest match. Consider adding an Oromo heritage id.

leads_only.name: Mascher Space Cooperative
leads_only.note: Community space at 1170 S Broad St where The Naked Stark runs its weekly drop-in and Falling Up workshop. Named on the group's own site, not checked.

leads_only.name: Philadelphia Youth Sports Collaborative
leads_only.note: Named as a partner for the Summer 2025 Quickball Community Play Days on The On Deck Circle's programs page, not checked.

leads_only.name: OLLAA (Oromo umbrella organization)
leads_only.note: Umbrella Oromo group that came up in a web search; may have a Pennsylvania chapter. Not checked.

notes: Deep pass on all seven groups. Pages that returned 404 (On Deck /2025-programs, Oromo /events and /about) are recorded as missing, not blocked. No page returned a bot check, paywall or 403. The Little Shul about page redirected to the homepage, which was already read. The Horizon take-action page contained embedded instructions, which were ignored. Budget: 1 of 1 WebSearch used and 33 WebFetch calls used out of 60.
